title: NEET protest: All SOPs followed, pellet gun use on protesters authorised - CRPF review
content: CRPF analysis indicates police action against protesters followed standard operating procedures.  Non-lethal means like pellet guns were authorized for crowd dispersal.  Force gradient was followed, with lower measures failing before pump action guns.  Protesters and personnel sustained injuries during the July 20 incident.  The matter is now sub judice before the Supreme Court.

title: After stalemate, government, opposition spar over paper leak law in Lok Sabha
content: Parliament debated a bill to strengthen penalties for exam paper leaks. Opposition members supported student protests and criticized police actions during demonstrations. Government speakers highlighted past paper leaks and PM Modi's reform efforts. They emphasized the bill's aim to protect student welfare and ensure fair examinations. The proposed law seeks to deter organized gangs and individuals involved in leaks.

title: CWG 2026: Gulveer Singh creates history, becomes first Indian to win Men's 10,000m medal
content: Gulveer Singh secured a historic silver medal in the men's 10,000m race. He became the first Indian to achieve this feat at the Commonwealth Games. Singh finished second behind Australia's Ky Robinson in Glasgow. The national record holder clocked a time of 27:49.78 during the event. This achievement marks a significant milestone for Indian athletics.

title: Trump, Netanyahu hold 'excellent' White House meeting as Iran differences come into focus
content: US President Trump and Prime Minister Netanyahu met at the White House to discuss Iran.  Both leaders sought to manage differences over the future course of the conflict.  They also discussed implementing a US-Israel framework agreement with Lebanon.  Discussions also covered expanding the Abraham Accords and Gaza stabilization efforts.  Both leaders face domestic political challenges and changing regional dynamics.

title: What made California's largest AI datacenter file a lawsuit over access to river water
content: California's largest AI data centre seeks Colorado River water after wastewater plans failed.  The company needs 287 million gallons annually for its proposed facility.  Local cities and the Imperial Irrigation District rejected its initial water requests.  This move raises concerns about the impact on regional farming and jobs.  The data centre promises economic benefits and construction employment opportunities.

title: Don't touch water bodies under garb of beautification, Supreme Court tells Bihar govt
content: The Supreme Court has ordered the Bihar government to stop filling historic ponds in Darbhanga.  This action follows allegations that the state is filling water bodies for public amenities.  The court warned the state not to touch the ponds without its explicit approval.  The project aimed to beautify and rejuvenate Gangasagar, Digghi, and Harahi Lake.  The Supreme Court directed the government to ensure the ponds' areas remain intact.

title: Defence minister Rajnath Singh unveils key policy reforms in Indian Coast Guard
content: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh introduced two key policy reforms for the Indian Coast Guard.  These reforms promote gender parity in officer induction and streamline ex-gratia payments.  Women candidates will now join the service on equal footing with male counterparts.  The new policies also accelerate compensation for families of missing personnel.  These changes aim to strengthen the morale and operational effectiveness of the force.

title: Delulu opposition thinks youth are with it, Rahul suffering from FOMO: NDA
content: BJP and allies defended the government's handling of student protests and paper leaks.  They asserted that the youth trust Prime Minister Modi's commitment to reforms.  Opposition leaders were criticized for using students for political gains and spreading cynicism.  The government highlighted its efforts to reform the education system and address concerns.  Measures were taken to clean the examination system after incidents occurred.

title: US man arrested for wiping phone during airport search; Android OS may trouble Europe travellers
content: A federal case in Atlanta questions privacy software use as criminal intent evidence. Prosecutors accuse Samuel Tunick of wiping his phone to prevent authorities from accessing its contents. GrapheneOS, a privacy-focused operating system, is central to the ongoing legal proceedings. Authorities in Europe also reportedly view GrapheneOS usage with suspicion. GrapheneOS developers state their software is legal and protects against unauthorized data extraction.

title: Congress, BJP spar over Pralhad Joshi's pick as education minister
content: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi criticized Pralhad Joshi's appointment as education minister. Gandhi accused Joshi of defending rapists in a past TV interview. BJP spokesperson Anil Baluni refuted these claims, stating Joshi commented on remission processes. Baluni accused Gandhi of distorting facts for personal attacks. The exchange highlights a political dispute over the minister's past statements.

title: Teen’s nuclear energy idea could cut Antarctic base emissions by 3,254 tons
content: A young Chilean student has proposed an innovative energy system for Antarctica. This concept combines renewable sources with a nuclear microreactor for reliable power.  The system aims to significantly reduce diesel fuel dependence and carbon emissions.  It offers a potential solution for powering remote research stations in extreme conditions.  This student-led idea highlights future possibilities for sustainable Antarctic energy.

title: How Europe's heatwave is proving Americans right about air conditioning
content: Europeans are now buying air conditioning units in unprecedented numbers. This trend is driven by record heatwaves and rising health concerns across the continent. Manufacturers report significant sales growth for cooling solutions in several European countries. Previously, air conditioning was viewed as an unnecessary luxury by many Europeans. This cultural shift reflects a growing understanding of cooling as an essential need.

title: Army showcases high-altitude combat capabilities, operational readiness in Ladakh
content: The Indian Army demonstrated its operational readiness in the Drass sector. This event celebrated the 27th Kargil Vijay Diwas and highlighted combat capabilities. Advanced technologies and drones were showcased during the live operational demonstration. The display featured various mobility and surveillance assets for mountainous terrain. This event paid tribute to soldiers who sacrificed during the Kargil conflict.

title: 1st direct freight train opens new India-Nepal chapter
content: India and Nepal have initiated a new era of rail connectivity. The first direct commercial container freight train arrived in Nepal last week. This new service is expected to significantly reduce transit times and logistics costs. The achievement builds upon the broad-gauge rail link inaugurated in June 2023. Direct freight movement to Biratnagar has now become operational, boosting bilateral trade.

title: Reports on alleged cybersecurity incident involving DRDO are incorrect: Sources
content: Official sources have denied reports of a cybersecurity incident involving DRDO data. Investigations found no evidence of active cyber attacks or unauthorized network intrusions. Most alleged leaked data is unclassified and from an old breach. Threat actors fabricated documents to appear recent and confidential for financial gain. The department stated the outdated data has no current relevance.

title: Nolan Wells' death probe deepens as witness alleges heavy drinking before tragedy
content: A new ABC News report says witnesses told investigators Nolan Wells had been drinking heavily before he disappeared on Horn Island on July 4. However, officials have not determined his cause of death. The official autopsy and toxicology results are still pending, while an independent autopsy listed the death as undetermined pending investigation. Ben Crump and Wells’ family continue to seek full answers.

title: Deebo Samuel's free agency heats up as top NFL teams emerge as contenders

Samuel seeks a team where he can contribute his physical, YAC-heavy style.  His market is driven by roster fit and timing rather than concerns.  A decision on his next team is expected soon.

title: Patrick and Brittany Mahomes' $1.625M gift creates new hope for Texas children
content: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes made a lasting impact off the football field with a $1.625 million partnership through the 15 and the Mahomies Foundation. Announced in October 2023, the initiative supports Boys & Girls Clubs in East Texas, Greater Kansas City and Lubbock, while also funding scholarships for hundreds of children and upgrading Club facilities. Here's how the Kansas City Chiefs star and his wife turned their hometown ties into a long-term commitment to help young people build brighter futures.

title: Ahmedabad tragedy: SC accepts pilot dad's plea not to make Air India crash report public

An NGO questioned the inquiry's impartiality and adherence to standard procedures. The Air Accident Investigation Bureau anticipates completing its investigation within six weeks. The final report is expected to be ready for distribution around October 2026.

title: Shipping min Sonowal says no Indian seafarer should be caught in crossfire

The government prioritizes the safety and welfare of Indian mariners serving on merchant vessels.  Officials reviewed security situations and diplomatic mission preparedness in conflict zones.  A union reported Indian sailors trapped in a Ukrainian port facing drone attacks.  Mental health support and pre-departure risk awareness programs were also emphasized.

content: Anahat Singh became the first Indian to win the World Junior Squash Championship. She chose to defer college, dedicating a year to her sport. This decision reflects her commitment to pursuing athletic excellence and future Olympic aspirations. Her journey highlights the importance of discipline and sacrifice in achieving significant goals. Anahat's success inspires young athletes across India to chase their dreams.

The leaders also explored efforts to restart stalled peace talks with Russia. Ukraine's president described the meeting as positive and productive for future support. title: India is second-largest sailor supplier in world

The report indicates India's share of global sailors has doubled over the past five years. Indian officers comprise thirteen point four percent of the world's officer workforce. This growth positions India strongly within the global maritime industry.

For the first time, an Indian private company has demonstrated the ability to develop and operate an orbital launch vehicle.
